fields.description: Five questions covering the same topics on every attempt. Pass with at least three correct.

fields.title: Find the 18th Century
fields.content:
The 18th century runs from 1701 to 1800. A year beginning with 17 usually belongs here, but the boundary matters: 1800 is still in the 18th century, while 1801 begins the 19th. Place a date before making a claim about its period. Our timeline is a modern learning tool, not an old calendar.

This mission introduces selected changes rather than every event in one hundred years. Compare trade connections, a temporary occupation and a government monopoly. They concern different parts of life and did not all begin together. An earlier event does not automatically cause a later one. Keep a question beside each date: what changed, where did it change, and what evidence supports the connection? You will investigate detailed reforms and new ideas in the later missions.

Open the three clues. Select a supported explanation. Use Explain for help and return to these clues before practice.

fields.title: Manila Was Connected by Trade
fields.content:
Manila was one end of the Manila-Acapulco galleon route. The Intramuros Administration dates this route from 1571 to 1815. It therefore existed before the 18th century and continued through it. The year 1815 belongs to the next century. A route can continue while other parts of life change.

Trade links show movement between places. They do not tell us that every household was wealthy or that everyone traded directly with Acapulco. A route map answers a question about connections; records about workers and households answer other questions. Imagine comparing a route card with a local household account. These are teaching examples, not surviving records supplied in this scene. Use each for the question it can support. Do not claim that international connections began only when a later policy was announced.

fields.title: A Temporary Change in Manila
fields.content:
The Intramuros Administration records a British occupation from 1762 to 1764 during the Seven Years War. This was a temporary political change in Manila. Political questions concern authority: who governed or controlled a place, and when? Locate the event on the same century timeline as the trade route.

Be careful about scale. Evidence about occupation in Manila does not prove that British forces governed every community throughout the islands. A capital city and an entire archipelago are not the same area. Nor does a temporary occupation establish permanent independence. Ask for the place and period whenever you explain control. You can investigate political change without reenacting a battle. No points are earned for harm; your task is to choose a statement that fits the source and identify what it does not establish.

fields.title: Government Rules Could Shape Work
fields.content:
The government tobacco monopoly was established in 1782 under Governor Jose Basco y Vargas. The National Tobacco Administration describes government efforts to raise revenue, or income for public authorities. This is an example of political decisions shaping economic activity: rules about a crop affected production and selling.

The same historical account describes compulsory planting, quotas and complaints in affected areas. A quota means a required amount. Do not assume every community grew the crop or that all farmers had identical experiences. Government income and household wellbeing are different questions. Study how a rule could limit choices rather than treating revenue as proof that everyone benefited. Tobacco is discussed only as historical evidence, not as a product to use. You will not grow, buy or try it in this learning activity.

fields.title: A Rule and Its Effects Are Different
fields.content:
A government can announce a rule before it is put into practice. The NHCP marker for the tobacco monopoly distinguishes a royal decree in 1780 from formal establishment in March 1782. These dates belong to different stages. Do not combine them into one date or assume that a decree immediately changed every local activity.

Use three investigation cards: decision, implementation and experience. A decree helps identify an official decision. An implementation record helps establish when a system started operating. Accounts of affected people help examine its effects. The cards here are modern teaching categories. A later account also reports abolition in 1882, outside this mission period; it must not be placed in the 18th century. In later missions you will compare reforms more closely. For now, distinguish what a government intended, what it put into practice and what people experienced.
